note: Scripture authority is the Open Word Bible (OWB), Amharic, Balanced edition (CC0), bundled as library/data/bible/owb-am-b.json.gz and read offline (owb-am). Every Scripture quotation was re-quoted to it verbatim (founder decision, 2026-11-18: Amharic quotes OWB everywhere), replacing the 1962/2003 UBS wording and the translator-rendered Old Testament verses the first edition carried.

A `mined` row is a verbatim OWB span in that block: the whole verse, the shortest contiguous span carrying the quoted clause, or exact OWB pieces joined with '…'; verbatim recitations without quote marks count (2 Cor 6:2, 1 Sam 16:7, Rom 8:18, Ps 27:1-3, Ps 27:14, Luke 18:19, James 1:17, Ps 8:4, 2 Cor 12:5, Acts 20:35, John 14:6, Matt 10:24, John 14:21). Citations follow the verse that holds the words: 'Watch and pray' Matt 26:41, 'all flesh is grass… and all its glory' 1 Pet 1:24, 'Be ye holy' Lev 19:2, 'there is no peace to the wicked' Isa 48:22, 'What is man that thou art mindful of him' Ps 8:4. The refrain 'Your will be done' is OWB's «ፈቃድህ ይሁን». Where Thomas's own sentence dwells on a quoted word the echo follows OWB (Luke 17:10's 'unprofitable servant', 1 Sam 3:9's 'Speak, Lord, for thy servant heareth').

`self_rendered` rows (each with a `why`) are the many allusions and Vulgate echoes woven into Thomas's sentences, and the places where his point rests on a Vulgate wording OWB (from the Hebrew) does not carry: Job 7:1 'warfare', Ps 85:8 'speak in me', Job 7:18 'visitest', Ps 30:10's past tense, Ps 120:5 'my sojourn is prolonged', Ps 25:17 'necessities', Isa 45:2-3, Ps 4:4. Same calls as the Japanese re-quote (PR #9897).
